title: Induced phenological avoidance: A neglected defense mechanism against seed predation in plants
screening_reason: Individual flower timing, predation, seed mass and plant total seed mass are measured in detail, and flowering is explicitly defined relative to the seed-predator activity period. However, the predator activity window is not recovered as an independently measured contemporaneous activity curve for each plant/year, so the study does not satisfy strict-H1 synchrony under the frozen timing contract.
notes: Geum urbanum × Byturus ochraceus; 59 plants in 2015 and an expanded sample in 2016, with flowering followed into 2017. Adult predators are described as active from late June to late July; predation is concentrated in the first flowering peak. Strong direct-seasonal-timing evidence with final seed-mass outcomes.
